messages:
Mia Chen: Heads-up — nightly CI perf run flagged a ~12% p99 latency regression on gpt-3-medium (dedicated pool). Summary attached from the job logs.
BenchBot: nightly-run/1742103456 finished: 1 failed threshold, 3 warnings. Link: https://ci.redwood/run/1742103456 :rotating_light:
Ajay Patel: ugh. I think this lines up with the kernel selector tweak from last week (PR #2897). We switched default -> fused-gemm-kernel for int8 paths.
Sofia Gomez: I kicked off a local replay harness (same prompt set as nightly) and see attention kernel times go up ~15ms per token at seq=512. Diff snippet below:
```
perf_summary: before -> after
attention_kernel_ms: 8.3 -> 23.7
matmul_ms: 4.1 -> 4.3
kv_lookup_ms: 1.2 -> 1.4
```
Luis Ortega: also noticing KV cache hit-rate dropped during the replay (was 98% -> 86%). Wondering if the harness isn't doing the same warmup that production traffic does.
Mia Chen: good catch. Nightly harness should run a KV warmup phase. Right now it's just steady-state synthetic traffic.
Nora Patel (SRE): CI alert fired correctly but this is probably noisy. Can we do a <apples-to-apples> baseline run so alerts are meaningful? Maybe add a rolling-window check and ignore single-run flakiness.
Ajay Patel: proposal: 1) add a dedicated apples-to-apples replay job that uses recorded request distribution (batch mix, seq-length histogram, same prompt prefixes). 2) Capture kernel-selection log and per-kernel timing histogram in artifacts. 3) Make nightly run include an explicit KV warmup pass (N requests or warm until hit-rate >= 95%).
Sofia Gomez: agreed. I have a golden replay set (replay/golden/2025-02-02) that we can use. Will run it against the failing commit and the previous stable to get an apples-to-apples comparison.
Luis Ortega: actionable snippet to run local harness with warmup:
```
./harness/replay --dataset replay/golden/2025-02-02 --warmup-requests 10000 --capture-kernels ./artifacts/kernels.json
```
Mia Chen: CI changes we need: - nightly -> run normal synthetic + warmup+apples-to-apples replay - persist kernel logs as artifact - threshold alert: switch to relative regression over the last 7 successful runs instead of absolute single-run thresholds - auto-open perf issue when regression >10% sustained for 3 runs
Nora Patel (SRE): I'll update the alerting rule. Suggest a 3-run rolling window and suppress if infra variance high. We'll also add a flaky-test label pipeline for failing perf jobs so triage isn't noisy.
Ajay Patel: I'll draft a PR to the CI job to add the replay step, kernel capture, and the warmup. Assigning to @Sofia for golden-set validation and @Luis for KV warmup tuning.
Sofia Gomez: running now, will paste perf diffs in this thread when done.
BenchBot: created perf-issue #452: "p99 regression gpt-3-medium — investigate kernel selection / KV warmup" (https://tracker.redwood/issues/452) :white_check_mark:
Luis Ortega: small note — when comparing kernels, we should force the kernel selector in one run to the old kernel to confirm causality: `export FORCE_KERNEL=gemm-v1` vs `FORCE_KERNEL=fused-gemm`.
Mia Chen: perfect. Also let's publish nightly artifacts to the perf dashboard after the job completes so product/eng can eyeball trends: dashboard link -> https://perf.redwood/dashboard/gpt-3-medium.
Nora Patel (SRE): adding chore: flaky-test triage docs + playbook for perf alerts. I'll own that. ETA EOD Friday.
Sofia Gomez: quick update — initial apples-to-apples replay confirms the fused kernel adds ~10-14% p99 on long sequences. Saving artifacts to s3://redwood-perf/artifacts/1742103456.
Mia Chen: next steps: Ajay PR to CI (due tomorrow), Sofia confirm golden-run diffs, Luis tune warmup and KV config, Nora update alerts/docs. We'll re-run nightly after PR merge and watch the 3-run window. Thanks all. :pray:
